[[Image:Bidensaristosa.jpg|thumb|right|205px|''Bidens aristosa'' seeds]]

'''''Bidens aristosa''''', known by many common names such as '''bearded beggarticks''', '''western tickseed''', '''showy tickseed''', '''long-bracted beggarticks''', '''tickseed beggarticks''', '''swamp marigold''', and '''Yankee lice''', is an [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]], [[annual plant|annual]] plant in the ''[[Asteraceae]]'' family. It is native to the [[central United States]], but has been introduced to the [[eastern United States]], [[Canada]], [[France]], [[Great Britain]], and [[India]]. It grows in [[Marsh|marshes]], [[Meadow|meadows]], pine forests and disturbed sites.

==Description==
''Bidens aristosa'' is a [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]], [[annual plant|annual]] [[flowering plant]] that typically grows between 1-2 ft tall, but can grow up to five feet tall. The leaves are attached to [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] 1 to 3 cm long. The leaf blades are [[lanceolate]] to lance-[[linear leaf|linear]], and are [[Laciniate|laciniately]] [[pinnatisect]]. It has numerous yellow [[flower heads]] with 5-10 [[ray florets]] and 12-40 [[disc floret]]s. Fruits are dry [[cypselae]] bearing barbs that get caught in fur or clothing, thus aiding in the plant's dispersal.<ref name=":fna">{{Cite web |last=Strother |first=John L. |last2=Weedon |first2=Ronald R. |title=''Bidens aristosa'' - FNA |url=http://floranorthamerica.org/Bidens_aristosa |access-date=6 December 2024 |website=Flora of North America}}</ref> 

==Distribution and habitat==
This species can be found from the [[United States]] ([[Alabama]], [[Arkansas]], [[District of Columbia]], [[Illinois]], [[Indiana]], [[Kentucky]], [[Louisiana]], [[Maryland]], [[Michigan]], [[Minnesota]], [[Missouri]], [[New York (state)|New York]], [[North Carolina]], [[South Carolina]], [[Tennessee]], [[Texas]], [[Virginia]], [[Wisconsin]]),<ref>{{BONAP|ref |genus=Bidens |species=aristosa}}</ref> [[Canada]] ([[Ontario]]), [[France]], [[Great Britain]], and [[India]].<ref name=":powo" /> 

The species is most likely native to the [[Central United States]], but has been introduced into the [[Eastern United States]], [[Central Canada]], France,<ref name=":inpn">{{Cite web |title=INPN - Inventaire national du patrimoine naturel (INPN) |url=https://inpn.mnhn.fr/espece/cd_nom/85939/tab/statut?lg=en |access-date=6 December 2024 |website=Inventaire national du patrimoine naturel}}</ref> Great Britain, and India. The first sighting of ''Bidens aristosa'' in the eastern United States was by the [[Potomac River]] near [[Glen Echo, Maryland|Glen Echo]], [[Maryland]] in 1902.<ref name="invasions">{{Cite web|title=''Bidens aristosa''|url=https://invasions.si.edu/nemesis/chesreport/species_summary/Bidens%20aristosa |access-date=12 February 2023|website= invasions.si.edu}}</ref> The species is likely spread by the import of food crops or wool products.<ref name="invasions" />

===Habitat===
''Bidens aristosa'' grows in [[marshes]], [[meadows]], pine forests and disturbed sites at elevations of 0 to 300 metres from [[sea level]].<ref name=":fna" />

==Taxonomy==
''Bidens aristosa'' was first described by [[André Michaux]] under the name ''Coreopsis aristosa'' in 1803 in the publication [[Flora Boreali-Americana]]. In 1893, [[Nathaniel Lord Britton]] moved the species to the genus ''Bidens'', while keeping the [[specific name|species epithet]] the same.<ref name=":tropicos">{{Cite web |title=Tropicos | Name - ''Bidens aristosa'' |url=https://www.tropicos.org/name/2709567 |access-date=6 December 2024 |website=Tropicos}}</ref>

===Etymology===
In English, this species is known by many common names. Common names include, but are not limited to; ''bearded beggarticks'', ''bur marigold'', ''long-bracted beggarticks'', ''swamp marigold'', ''tickseed beggarticks'', ''western tickseed'', ''Yankee lice'', ''midwestern beggarticks,'' and ''showy tickseed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Showy Tickseed |url=https://roundstoneseed.com/native-wildflowers/11-showy-tickseed.html |website=Roundstone Native Seed Company |language=en}}</ref>''<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Bidens aristosa'' (Bearded Beggarticks,, Bur Marigold, Long-Bracted Beggarticks, Long-Bracted Tickseed Sunflower, Swamp Marigold, Tick Seed, Tickseed Beggarticks, Tickseed Sunflower, Western Tickseed, Yankee Lice) | North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/bidens-aristosa/ |access-date=2024-12-06 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref><ref name=":usda">{{Cite web |title=USDA Plants Database Plant Profile General |url=https://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile/BIAR |access-date=6 December 2024 |website=USDA Plants Database}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=''Bidens aristosa'' (midwestern beggar-ticks): Go Botany |url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/bidens/aristosa/ |access-date=2024-12-06 |website=gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org}}</ref>
